parole.testo: From Byzantine Greek κασοῦλα (kasoûla), from Latin casula (“hooded cloak”). Doublet of kaçule. Compare also Romanian căciulă. Attested in 1417 (Catasto Veneto di Scutari) as "Chisolichochi" (i.e. Kësolëkoqi, modern Kësulëkuqi, "bearing a red riding hood", masc.).

Shortening of *qiftër, from Byzantine Greek ξιφτέρι, ἐξιφτέριν (xiphtéri, exiphtérin), from Latin accipiter (“hawk”). According to Orel, borrowed directly from Latin accipiter (“vulture”), for the loss of the last syllable see mbret. Doublet of skifter.
Reduced form of variant rrushajë, from Byzantine Greek ῥουσάλια (rhousália), from Latin rōsālia.
From Byzantine Greek τράπεζα (trápeza, “table”), via a borrowing from dialectal Latin *trabeza.
